paragraphs.text: Today, we're going to the lab to do some practical work.
The lab was a big room with long tables, chairs, and big cupboards.
There were white mice in cages.
When Mr. Kent walked by their cages, they all started running around and making a lot
Laughed, Mr. Kent, speaking to the white mice.
Then he looked at the class and said, Today's lesson is about worms.
I'm going to give you some worms, and you have to cut them in half.
The two pieces can live and move by themselves.
I didn't want to cut it.
Karen, are you afraid of your worm?
Give me your knife, and I can help you.
His arm touched mine, and I got an electric shock.
I jumped up from my chair.
Oh, nothing, nothing, I said, trying to smile.
He cut the worm and then walked to the next table to help other students.
I wrote a note to Walter and told him about the electric shock.
He turned around and I gave him the note.
Walter and Karen, what are you doing?
What do you have in your hand, Walter?
Walter and I were in big trouble with the teacher.
Next time, you'll have to give me the note.
When the science lesson was over, Mr. Kent called me to his desk.
I'm sorry I scared you during the lesson.
Two years ago, I had a bad car accident and lost my arm.
At lunch, I told Walter and Barbara about Mr. Kent's electric arm.
As we walked out of the cafeteria, we saw Mr. Wilkinson.
He said, looking at us, his eyes were green again, but I didn't say anything.
At half past three, Walter and I ran out of the school and waited for Mr. Wilkinson to
We saw a lot of students and teachers, but we didn't see him.
Finally, we saw him walking down the street, and we followed him silently.
He lived near the school in a pretty white house.
There was a small garden around it and a big tree near the front door.
He walked into his house and we went quietly to a window and looked inside.
He put some books on the kitchen table and opened the refrigerator.
He took out a bottle of the horrible green juice and put it on the table.
I can climb up this tree.
Don't forget, I go rock climbing.
I climbed up the tree and I could see Mr. Wilkinson's bedroom.
He's in his bedroom and he's sitting in front of a mirror.
His hands are on his hair.
I continued looking into the house.
Mr. Wilkinson was now completely bald.
Suddenly I saw my face in Mr. Wilkinson's mirror and he saw it too.
He turned around and looked at me.
I was terrified and I didn't know what to do.
I could not run away because I was at the top of a big tree.
But Mr. Wilkinson didn't look angry.
He walked over and opened the window.
Karen, what are you doing up this tree?
I want to talk to you.
I climbed down the tree and Walter was waiting for me.
Mr. Wilkinson wants to talk to us.
Mr. Wilkinson came out of his house and stood in the garden.
Let me tell you my story.
Last year, my doctor told me I was very ill.
I had an operation and then chemotherapy.
After the operation, I lost my voice.
So now I speak with a type of artificial voice.
That's why my voice sounds strange.
I lost all my hair from the chemotherapy.
So now I wear a wig.
Mr. Wilkinson, we're very sorry about our terrible behavior.
Yes, please forgive us, I said.
I am getting better now, which is good.
May I ask you a question?
What's that green juice you drink at lunch?
The green juice and the black pills are medicines.
But why do your eyes change color?
So you saw that, did you?
I wanted to do something different.
So I bought a pair of colored contact lenses.
I thought a new look could make me feel better.
Did the contact lenses make you feel better?
Mr. Wilkinson looked at me and smiled.
It was nice having something different for a day.
But it's my job that is really making me feel better.
You like your job, don't you?
It's wonderful to work with young people like you.
It's a beautiful city with lots of parks and fun things to do.
And I'm starting to make a few friends.
